findings.field: authoredCatalog.members[0..7].mutation ("Index 1 is the occupancy v2 namedCorpusClasses[0].exactByteIntent sentence for that surface, quoted") read against the eight surface fixture files
findings.title: Six of the eight surface cells do not quote the exactByteIntent sentence they claim to quote, and the truncation is governed by two incompatible rules, so no stated or inferable rule re-derives the eight index-1 strings from occupancy v2.
measured: All eight index-1 strings are byte-exact substrings of occupancy v2 namedCorpusClasses[0].exactByteIntent. Nothing is invented. The defect is that the member field describes them as the 'sentence' and they are, in six cases, not the sentence.
human and JSON quote the complete source sentence including its terminal period: 'Human and JSON cells retain host-owned projections of the same structured envelope.' (83 bytes, exact).

SARIF, doctor, fault, config and log stop at the semicolon and drop the sentence's second clause. Dropped tails, verbatim: SARIF '; they do not restore G17 advertised-parity fixtures and do not execute harness.DR-G26.preview-analyze-sarif-not-advertised.'; doctor '; they do not author G12 FC implementations, doctor schema, D9 mapping, or purge.'; fault '; they do not execute G21 crash/panic/timeout/resource/malformed/truncated/duplicate/EOF/process-tree/recovery.'; config '; they do not invent DR-108 storage mechanics and do not score G09 requested/granted/denied tables.'; log '; they do not admit unstructured host logs.'

progress is the decisive case. Its source sentence 'Progress cells retain host-owned progress/status projection of component-emitted progress.' contains no semicolon, so the semicolon rule cannot apply — yet the fixture still drops the terminal period, giving an 89-byte string where the sentence is 90 bytes.

The two rules are mutually exclusive against the same class. Under 'quote the whole sentence' (which human and JSON obey, period included) progress is wrong. Under 'quote up to the first terminal punctuation, exclusive' (which progress obeys) human and JSON are wrong. No third rule stated anywhere in the subject covers all eight.

The subject states the convention four times — in authorityClaim, in whatIsAuthored, in sarifCellStanding.corpusSpeaker ('quotes the occupancy exactByteIntent non-advertisement sentence') and in all eight member mutation fields — and every statement uses 'sentence'. None discloses truncation, none states a semicolon rule, and none accounts for progress.

This is the first artifact in docs/coop/artifacts/ to author quotation cells: 'two-element JSON array' and 'exactByteIntent sentence' each occur only in this subject. There is no prior accepted usage in which 'sentence' has been established to mean 'clause', so the term cannot be read loosely on precedent.
findings.whyItMatters: The corpus's entire evidentiary value is that each cell is a byte-exact quotation witness re-derivable from a frozen upstream. A later remasurement that reads the member field and mechanically extracts 'the exactByteIntent sentence for that surface' reproduces two of eight cells and mismatches six, and the mismatch is indistinguishable from fixture drift because the file carries no rule that would explain it. Recording these digests under a description their bytes contradict freezes that ambiguity into the record.
findings.notClaimed: This is not an invention finding and not a contradiction of occupancy v2. Every byte is quoted from the frozen source, the surface set is complete and ordered, and the dropped clauses are the specification's exclusion clauses, whose omission from a fixture payload may well be deliberate and correct. The defect is that the subject never says so.
findings.repairShape: Either state the derivation rule explicitly and make it uniform across all eight cells — e.g. 'index 1 is the retention clause of the exactByteIntent sentence for that surface, taken up to but excluding the first semicolon or terminal period' with progress and human/JSON brought under that single rule — or keep the bytes and change the six member fields plus the four summary statements to say 'clause' and name the truncation. Which of the two is a fixture-byte question and is the author's to decide; I did not edit the subject or any fixture.

advisories.note: The subject justifies the flat no-platform-subdirectory shape on the g21.v1 precedent, but a sibling gate whose platform list it verifies as ORDERED-EQUAL went the other way: docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/g23.v4/ is organised as linux-arm64, linux-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64 subdirectories, and g23.v3/v4 are both named in doesNotMutate, so the divergent precedent was in view. Occupancy v2 passProperty requires a cell 'on all four D-002 platforms' and 'Pass all four D-002 platforms', so a complete authoring is 8x4=32 surface cells; this corpus authors 8. I do not treat this as blocking: the deferral is disclosed in four places (whatIsNotAuthored, remainderAfterThisCorpus, proposedLaterWork, doesNot), OBL-G20-FX-AUTHORING is explicitly left open, and D-293 Decision 8 delegates exactly this kind of underdetermined choice. Naming the g23 shape and saying why g21's was chosen would close the question for the recording reviewer.

Recorded so a later reviewer does not over-read my recomputation. My encoder reproduced the fixtures' stage-coverage commitment exactly, which is the only commitment the subject claims. It did not reproduce delivery.v2's own requestedCoverageDomain.domainCommitment sha256:9e1101a1… under any of four candidate value shapes I tried (keys array, keys[0], the requestedCoverageDomain map without its commitment, and a stageId/relations/keys map) across three key orderings. delivery.v2 is a pinned upstream that this candidate quotes rather than re-decides, and the subject asserts nothing about that commitment, so this is not a defect in the subject; I simply did not determine that domain's committed value shape and make no claim about it either way.

NT-4's input names five attempt-tokens (policyOutcome, verdict, threshold, waiver, gate) and the corpus witnesses one; NT-7's input names two forms (planAdmission, RequestId/ExecutionId allocation) and the corpus witnesses one. The remainder section does not name the unexercised alternatives. I opened this as a candidate finding and then refuted it on precedent: g21-fixture-corpus.v1 NT-2 does exactly the same thing (its input names findings/finding/verdict/threshold/waiver and the fixture witnesses 'findings' alone) and its remainder is likewise silent, and that corpus was recorded at D-241. Consistent with accepted precedent, so advisory only.

g20-named-corpus-catalog.v2 still carries fixtureBytes 'NOT-AUTHORED' for this class, and those bytes now exist on disk. The subject's role text describes that standing accurately as the catalog's own frozen claim and says it 'consumes that naming', which is correct as far as it goes. What it does not say is that recording this corpus makes the catalog's NOT-AUTHORED assertion stale as an authoring claim. The idiom already exists in this lineage — g20-leftover-join.v6 leftoverDesignOpenStanding uses 'stale as an authoring claim' and 'stale as a naming claim' for the specification and initial-state claims — and proposedLaterWork item 2 uses it for the joins but not for the catalog. A one-line statement would keep the catalog's standing legible to the recording entry.
